newsitem.title: USA: Mortgage rates fall in week.
newsitem.headline: Mortgage rates fall in week.

text.p: Mortgage rates fell this week as inflation fears subsided on Wall Street, causing bond yield to move lower, the Federal Home Loan Mortgage Corp. said Thursday.

Thirty-year fixed-rate mortgage rates averaged 8.28 percent in the week ended Sept. 13, down from 8.34 percent last week. Fifteen-year mortgages also fell to an average of 7.81 percent from 7.88 percent last week.
But one-year adjustable mortgage rates inched up to 5.90 percent from 5.85 percent.
A year ago, the 30-year rate averaged 7.60 percent, the 15-year 7.12 percent, and the adjustable loan 5.80 percent.
"This week's figures reflect an element of stability in the bond market after fears of inflation caused interest rates to rise last week," Freddie Mac Chief Economist Robert Van Order said.

"Recent news that housing prices have risen at an annualized rate of 4.1 percent nationally coupled with interest rates in the affordable eight to 8.5 percent range makes homeownership even more attractive, which should translate into a good year for home sales," he added.

Freddie Mac said lenders charged an average of 1.7 percent in fees and points on 30-year loans and 1.4 percent on adjustable loans, both unchanged from last week. Charges on 15-year mortgages rose to 1.7 percent from 1.6 percent.
Separately, the Mortgage Bankers Association of America said new mortgage applications fell 26.0 percent in the week ended Sept. 6.
Specifically, the volume of applications to refinance mortgages fell 36 percent, while applications to purchase mortgages dipped 23.5 percent.
